tests.name: collinearity_vif_test
tests.comparison: Variance Inflation Factor of up_day_ratio_20 in a multivariate model containing mom_20 and up_day_ratio_20 as predictors of ruin outcome
tests.success_criterion: VIF for up_day_ratio_20 < 5, confirming it captures non-redundant variance beyond mom_20
tests.failure_criterion: VIF for up_day_ratio_20 >= 5, indicating proxy redundancy and that the researcher's mechanism conflates momentum decomposition with independent signal

tests.name: volatility_normalized_pullback_test
tests.comparison: Normalized pullback depth (pullback_pct / vol_ratio_5_20) between false_positive_ruin and selected_winner cases
tests.success_criterion: False_positive_ruin normalized pullback depth is significantly shallower than selected_winner (Mann-Whitney p < 0.10), supporting mechanism claim that vol_ratio does not merely proxy baseline volatility
tests.failure_criterion: No significant difference in normalized pullback depth between groups, indicating the apparent failure pattern is a trivial artifact of heterogeneous volatility baselines

tests.name: moment_variance_interaction_test
tests.comparison: Ruin rate conditioned on mom_20 quartile and vol_ratio_5_20 threshold (1.40) cross-tabulation
tests.success_criterion: Within the lowest mom_20 half (<= 0.14), high vol_ratio_5_20 (>1.40) shows ruin rate >50% vs <20% for low vol_ratio_5_20; within the highest mom_20 half, vol_ratio_5_20 does not predict ruin (demonstrating interaction, not main effect)
tests.failure_criterion: Vol_ratio_5_20 predicts ruin regardless of mom_20 level, or mom_20 fully mediates vol_ratio_5_20 effect, indicating vol_ratio is not an independent mechanism

tests.name: within_snapshot_consistency_test
tests.comparison: Outcome proportions for up_day_ratio_20 x vol_ratio_5_20 cell within each snapshot, then aggregated
tests.success_criterion: The up_day_ratio_20 x vol_ratio_5_20 effect direction is consistent across >=3 distinct snapshots (sign test p < 0.10), ruling out snapshot-concentration artifact
tests.failure_criterion: Effect direction reverses or disappears in >50% of snapshots, indicating the pooled pattern arises from snapshot heterogeneity rather than a stable predictor

tests.name: threshold_sensitivity_bootstrap_test
tests.comparison: Ruin rate at researcher's proposed thresholds (0.60, 1.40) versus ±0.05 perturbations, evaluated via leave-one-out cross-validation across snapshots
tests.success_criterion: Ruin rate difference between cells remains >=10 percentage points when thresholds vary ±0.05 in any direction (robustness to threshold selection)
tests.failure_criterion: Ruin rate difference collapses to <5 percentage points when thresholds shift ±0.05, indicating the pattern is an artifact of threshold optimization on N=27

leakage_checks: pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks are excluded from all test feature sets—they are post-snapshot measurements that would introduce forward-looking bias if used to predict ruin
Feature computation for up_day_ratio_20, mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, and MA slopes must be completed at snapshot time, not retroactively reconstructed from post-entry price series
Threshold derivation must be pre-specified before inspecting within-snapshot ruin counts to prevent threshold optimization on outcome-concentrated snapshots
Cross-snapshot validation uses outcome labels computed identically across all snapshots—snapshot identity must not influence how outcomes are classified
Interaction test uses only pre-snapshot features (mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20) to predict post-snapshot outcomes—no outcome information leaks into feature computation
